text.content:
Equipment has evolved following the growth of technology in Ardor in the three different classifications of technology: Archaeotechnology, Arcanotechnology, and Sygican Technology. While these terms typically refer to large devices, appliances and machinery, adventuring or combat gear in Ardor will fall into these three categories as well, though the distinction is seldomly important, mostly from a narrative perspective unless one is playing an Empty.

As Immortal Ardor borrows from both Pathfinder and Starfinder mechanics, it is important to assume that in most cases, the archaic, tech or analog trait have no final bearing on the strength or capabilities of a piece of equipment as much as the statblock of the item or other traits it may have.

Archaeotech Equipment

Archaeotech equipment is completely mundane and does not operate on the use of magic; it runs entirely on its own or uses non-magical sources of fuel or power (such as oil or steam). Gear that is built from archaeotech is typically any form of standard weapons or armor. In these cases, quality and properties are what determines a weapon or armor’s capabilities, as listed under High-Quality gear variants (Pathfinder Gamemastery Guide) or weapon, armor or shield grades (Starfinder Player Core). For them to remain archaeotech, their upgrade equivalents for property runes would be non-magical upgrades. While archaeotechnology itself flourishes, gear that is completely mundane or does not eventually veer into sygicatech territory is rare.

In Starfinder, these would be non-magical items with the archaic trait, or non-magical analog or tech items.  If these pieces of gear were upgradeable further due to their construction through runes or magic-based sygican upgrades, they would be considered arcanotech or sygicatech, depending on their nature. Anyone, including Empty, can use all forms of archaeotech devices or gear with little issue as they are non-magical.

Arcanotech Equipment

Arcanotech equipment contains magical properties and is often activated through the use of ether. If it bears some form of magical circuitry or enchantment, the magic is what gives it its properties. Gear that is arcanotech is among the most commonplace and is the assumed default in Ardor as it relies on magical crafting, enchantments or applications of runes on their material. Arcanotech equipment benefits from all forms of spell and magic-related crafting and creation, including through feats and rituals such as Aspektus Enchanting, runecrafting, or soulforging.

In Starfinder, these would be magical Pathfinder items with the archaic and magical traits. In many instances, magical items like these are also invested items. Empty can’t use or benefit from all but the simplest arcanotech devices or equipment, especially if the item requires investment or is activated by Casting a Spell or Envisioning, or requiring any form of ether to use.

Sygicatech Equipment

Sygicatech equipment proliferated with the arrival of the sygican people from Garrunga to the Ardorean mainland. These weapons are operated by mundane means or utilize a fuel source, but possess the ability to empower their weapons through magic that is grafted into their make. Sygicatech gear is developed to bridge the gap between ether-bearing and Empty adventurers, and thus it often bears magical circuitry that activates a continuous or a single-fire effect. In Sygicatech items this circuitry is called an Engram, and activating them uses the @UUID[Compendium.immortal-ardor.feats.PwrR4w8fCpUevqWc]{Ingrave} action, which is typically an Interact action to operate its mechanisms to energize the engram’s effects. Ingraving usually requires the fuel source the piece of equipment might have, which is typically some form of etheric battery or sygican fuel core. A piece of equipment might have multiple Engrams, but a single battery can supply the fuel needed for all of its Engrams.

In Starfinder, these items would bear the analog or tech trait, as well as the magical trait. All Sygicatech gear has the Sygican trait. Anyone, including Empty can use Sygicatech equipment, and Empty frequently have easier access to this equipment. Starfinder @UUID[Compendium.sf2e-anachronism.equipment.5PS5ESGpnQfJNOdg]{Batteries} act as the etheric batteries (the ammo-based consumable) or sygican fuel cores (for larger devices).

Seekers of Ardor revamps the types of equipment available to spellcasters, by allowing magical implements to be strongly defined. It introduces new types of equipment in the form of Scepters and spell runes and adjusts the way Wands and Staves function. More information is available in the Implements of Magic section in the Equipment chapter.

Magical implements are equipment that are meant to be used by spellcasters as they influence their spellcasting abilities or allow them to cast spells through them. Wands, Scepters and Staves are examples of these implements. Typically, these implements are activated by using the Cast a Spell activity.

Magical implements can be engraved with runes in the same way weapons and armor can. While some implements can function like a weapon, allowing them to be inscribed with weapon runes, they also can be inscribed with spell runes, which are runes that are specific to magical implements. Spell runes and weapon runes are mutually exclusive unless stated otherwise. Rules for spell runes are provided in their specific section below.

Some implements such as wands with fundamental spell runes, scepters and staves must be prepared and charged during daily preparations, which gives a spellcaster full access to the functionalities of the implement. A spellcaster can only charge one implement for use each day.

Barring any adjustments specifically detailed here, Wands and Staves follow their respective rules.

Spell Runes

Spell runes are runes that apply specifically to magical implements. These runes provide improvements and benefits to spellcasters who wield these items. Like weapon runes, they have fundamental spell runes as well as property spell runes. All rules for spell runes follow the guidelines for how weapon runes work, from inscribing, transferring, or crafting runes onto magical implements.

When using a magical implement with spell runes, its benefits only apply to the spells within the implement. A wand of Fireball with a widening property rune would only confer its effect to the fireball cast with its charge, and a staff of fire with a spell potency rune would similarly only apply its spell attack bonus to a cast of Ignition from the staff.

However, magical implements with runes can be invested into by a spellcaster that charges them. When invested, the spell runes on the magical implement can apply to all spells cast by the spellcaster that is wielding them on hand, though some runes apply only to specific spells or have requirements which must be met. As a spellcaster can only charge one magical implement each day, they can only invest into one of these implements.

Fundamental Spell Runes include spell potency runes and spell versatility runes. When inscribed with them, a magical implement must be prepared and charged and then wielded by the spellcaster who charged it for them to benefit from the runes’ effects. A potency rune grants you an item bonus to your spell attack for spells you cast by the value on the potency rune (+1, +2, and +3) while wielding a charged implement. A versatility rune has different effects depending on what implement it is inscribed into, but generally improves upon the primary benefit of a particular implement.

  • For wands, it allows you to have an extra charge of the spell on the wand.

  • For scepters, it allows the scepter to hold another spell.

  • For staves, it grants you additional charges when you charge the staff.

Property Spell Runes behave similar to property runes in weapons and armor; you can engrave a number of property runes to a magical implement equal to the value of the potency rune. These confer unique effects that range from improving spells cast from the implement, improving spellcasting in general, or turning the implement into a capable fighting weapon.

Wands

With the addition of spell runes, most specialized wands are treated as if they possess a spell property rune, even though they do not possess any fundamental runes. At a GM’s discretion, specialized wands could come with fundamental runes to behave like any engraved wand, but this would increase their gold value for the purposes of treasure awards.

When engraved with fundamental spell runes, a wand needs to be prepared and charged for its wielder to benefit from the runes’ inscribed effects. This doesn’t prevent a spellcaster from using other wands, but they cannot benefit from an unprepared wand’s fundamental runes. A spell versatility rune grants the wand an additional charge to cast its spell, depending on the rank of the spell and the rank of the rune.

Staves

Staves normally only allow spells to be cast from it at the rank they’re presented in the staff’s stat block, disallowing it from being heightened. This rule has been altered so that you can cast spells from the staff at a heightened level, as long as you spend the charges to cast it at the appropriate spell rank, up to the maximum spell rank available to the staff. Any spells that are repeated at higher ranks on a given staff can be replaced with similar thematic spells.

While a staff can be inscribed with weapon runes, it can also instead be inscribed with spell runes. A spell versatility rune grants a staff additional charges when it is charged during daily preparations equal to the rank of the rune.

Scepters

Seekers of Ardor introduces a new type of equipment in the form of Scepters.

A scepter is a type of magical implement. Each day during daily preparations, you can charge a scepter; when you do, you add a spell from your repertoire or a spell you can prepare for it to hold. Once during the day, you can cast a spell held by a scepter you charge at any rank you can cast at. Once this charge is expended, you can only cast a held spell again by spending a spell slot or a prepared spell at the rank of the spell expended.

A scepter can be inscribed with weapon runes, which would increase its power as a regular weapon would. However, it can also be inscribed with spell runes instead. A spell versatility rune allows you to hold additional spells in the scepter equal to the rank of the rune (though it does not grant an additional charge).
